## Proposed change

The slot suspension repair currently guesses between two very different causes:

> The lock may be rejecting the code silently **or** experiencing communication issues.

Lock Code Manager has no reliable way to tell those apart from the lock's behaviour alone — both present identically from the slot's point of view: a code that was written and never reads back.

Providers that can measure their own transport do know, though. This adds an optional `describe_link_health()` hook on `BaseLock` (default `None`) whose sentence is appended to that repair.

It is deliberately **descriptive only** — nothing reads it to make a decision, no new state, no thresholds, no control-flow change. A provider that cannot measure anything returns `None` and the repair keeps its existing wording verbatim. Each implementation reports *measurements*, never a verdict, and states the semantics of what it reports so the reader is not misled by them.

### Z-Wave JS

Quotes the node's own counters:

> Z-Wave link, counted since Z-Wave JS started or the statistics were last reset: 256 commands reached this lock, 4 could not be sent at all, and 126 read requests went unanswered; recent round trips averaged 1072 ms.

All three counters appear separately rather than as a ratio, because node-zwave-js counts them over different populations (verified against `NodeStatistics.ts`): `commandsTX` counts only commands *successfully sent* (`:47`) — an out-of-range lock increments `commandsDroppedTX` (`:54`) instead — while `timeoutResponse` counts only Get-type commands (`:55`). Any single ratio built from these distorts in the exact case the feature exists for. `rtt` is an exponential moving average (`:59-61`), so it is reported as an average, and the window wording covers resets as well as restarts (`:44`).

### ZHA

Zigbee has no per-node failure counters — zigpy keeps counters on the radio application, not per device — so ZHA reports the other honest signal:

> Zigbee link, from the last frame this lock sent: signal quality 12 of 255, -89 dBm, last heard from 3 hours ago.

Staleness carries most of the weight: a lock not heard from in hours while LCM is actively writing to it is the Zigbee equivalent of an unanswered-command count, and it stays meaningful on radios reporting no signal metrics. `lqi`/`rssi` are overwritten from each received packet, so the wording says "the last frame this lock sent" rather than implying an average.

### Providers deliberately left out

- **Matter** — Thread/WiFi diagnostics clusters *are* subscribed, but the packet and error counters are optional per spec (gated on the `PKTCNT`/`ERRCNT` feature bits) and read all-zero in the only available node fixture. Shipping a sentence built on counters that may always be zero would reproduce exactly the misleading output this PR exists to avoid. Needs validation against real hardware first.
- **zigbee2mqtt** — publishes `linkquality` per device, but the provider does not retain it; capturing it would mean new per-lock state for a point-in-time value with no staleness signal.
- **Schlage / Akuvox** — cloud APIs with no radio link telemetry.
- **virtual** — nothing to measure.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- This PR is related to issue: #1397

Motivated by #1397, where the reporter's lock left ~49% of the commands sent to it unanswered (126 of 256 cumulative; 19 of 39 during a controlled test). The write reached the lock — the PIN works on the keypad — but the driver's post-write verification read timed out, so the value database kept serving a stale `userIdStatus = Available` and the slot could never confirm. It looked exactly like a silently rejected code.

Note this does **not** close #1397: the reporter's underlying problem is their Z-Wave mesh, not integration logic. It makes the next report of this shape self-diagnosing.

Coverage remains at 100%.

content.text:
Researched all six providers against their underlying libraries. **One had usable data; I added it. Three didn't; one I deliberately skipped.**

## Added — ZHA

Zigbee has no per-node failure counters (zigpy keeps counters on the radio *application*, not per device), so it reports the other honest signal:

> Zigbee link, from the last frame this lock sent: signal quality 12 of 255, −89 dBm, last heard from 3 hours ago.

Reachable with **no new state**: `cluster.endpoint.device` off the already-cached DoorLock cluster — both accessors verified public in zigpy. `lqi`/`rssi`/`last_seen` all live on `zigpy.Device` (`:98`, `:99`, `:222`).

Staleness does the real work here. A lock unheard-from for hours while LCM is writing to it is the Zigbee equivalent of an unanswered-command count, and it survives radios that report no signal metrics — so each value is emitted only if present.

## Deliberately skipped — Matter

This is the judgment call worth flagging. Thread/WiFi diagnostics clusters **are** subscribed — the lock fixture carries 68 Thread attributes including `TxAckRequestedCount`/`TxAckedCount`, which is exactly the sent-vs-acknowledged signal I'd want. But:

- the packet/error counters are **optional per spec**, gated on the `PKTCNT`/`ERRCNT` feature bits
- every one reads **0** in the only fixture available, and `WiFiNetworkDiagnostics` has just `WiFiVersion` populated

I can't tell whether that's the mock or real device behavior. Shipping on it would risk printing "0 of 0 commands" *plus* a confident mesh assertion — the precise failure the review just caught in the Z-Wave version. Needs real hardware to validate first.

## Not available

- **zigbee2mqtt** — publishes `linkquality`, but the provider doesn't retain it; capturing means new per-lock state for a point-in-time value with no staleness signal
- **Schlage / Akuvox** — cloud APIs, no radio telemetry
- **virtual** — nothing to measure

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The three transports give structurally different evidence: Z-Wave gives cumulative *failure counts*, Zigbee gives a point-in-time *sample plus staleness*, Matter would give *device-side self-report*. That's why a shared numeric metric on `BaseLock` would have been wrong — a `link_quality: float` field would have forced all three into one scale that means something different in each. Returning a sentence lets each say the true thing.
- Skipping Matter is the same discipline as dropping the ratio: the review's lesson was that a number whose semantics you haven't verified is worse than no number, because it arrives wearing the authority of a measurement.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Verification:** 1432 passed / 3 skipped, coverage **100.00%**, `prek` exit 0. Four new ZHA tests (full metrics, staleness-only, nothing-measured, unresolvable cluster). PR description updated to document both implementations and the exclusions with reasoning.

def describe_link_health(self) -> str | None:
        """
        Report the lock's own Thread radio counters.

        Two numbers, both read straight from Thread Network Diagnostics:
        acknowledged transmissions out of those that asked to be
        acknowledged, and how many times the lock has dropped off the Thread
        network. The first pair is safe to state as a proportion because
        both counters are drawn from the same population -- unlike most
        counter pairs in this cluster, where the numerator and denominator
        count different traffic and a ratio would quietly mislead.

        feature bits), so each is read independently and simply omitted when
